title: Acme Corp — Savings simulation and Optimize recommendations (Q3)
content:
Summary:
This sheet is a customer-specific before/after simulation for Acme Corp showing expected monthly cost impact after applying Redwood Optimize recommendations. This is intended to support a commercial proposal and an optional pilot. Preliminary headline: expected steady-state monthly inference spend drops from $82.6k to ~$34.9k under the recommended bundle (approx. 58% savings) in the canonical workload scenario.

Context & objective:
- Customer: Acme Corp — multi-tenant product search + assistant feature across web and mobile.
- Current infra: Hosted endpoints, mixed model set (open LLM variants + a proprietary reranker), no consistent batching, no KV prefix cache, single-region hosting (us-west).
- Objective: quantify savings if Acme adopts a Redwood Optimize package (batching rules, KV caching, quantized model variants, autoscale tuning, and route fallbacks). Provide conservative/expected/optimistic scenarios and sensitivity to traffic growth.

Key assumptions (derived from Acme telemetry and infra invoices):
- 30-day active window; monthly request count: 13.2M requests (~440k/day).
- Avg prompt+completion length: 120 tokens (70 prompt, 50 completion).
- Current average effective concurrency (p99): 220 active requests.
- Current stack: unbatched GPU endpoints running fp16 variants; per-token effective unit cost (compute + infra amortized): $0.0000625/token (implied current monthly compute ~$82.6k).
- Baseline network/overhead and storage unchanged. We only model inference compute + dedicated capacity line items.

Baseline (Before Redwood Optimize):
- Monthly tokens = 13.2M req * 120 tokens = 1.584B tokens/month.
- Effective per-token cost = $0.0000522 (calculated from invoices + allocated infra) -> monthly = 1.584B * $0.0000522 = $82,647 (matches invoices).
- Observed inefficiencies: low batching (avg batch size = 1.8), 0% KV prefix cache for repeated prompts, suboptimal autoscale (overprovision at peak -> idle GPU minutes), and heavy use of full-precision kernels.

Recommendations (bundle):
1) Continuous batching policy: increase avg batch size to 6.0 for steady-state traffic while preserving p95 latency SLOs (route-level config + jittering).
2) KV prefix caching: implement 3-tier prefix cache for stable prompts (expected 18% hit-rate of tokens reduced to near-zero compute).
3) Quantized served model variants: move warm routes to 8-bit/4-bit quantized variants where quality impact is minimal (LLM-13b-q4/8).
4) Autoscale policy tuning: reduce baseline reserved GPUs by 25% and use burst pools to cover spikes.
5) Smart routing + fallback: route tail/experimental flows to cheaper variants under load.

Estimated impact per recommendation (expected case):
- Batching: reduces effective per-token energy overhead ~20% (operationally equivalent to 14% cost reduction overall) because less kernel launch overhead and better GPU utilization.
- KV cache: with 18% hit-rate on prefixes and average prefix length 30 tokens, effective token compute reduction ~5.4% (0.18 * 30/120).
- Quantization: moves cost per token for targeted routes from baseline to ~40% of fp16 cost (approx 60% reduction on quantized portion). We conservatively apply quantization to 45% of tokens.
- Autoscale: reduces idle/overprovision costs by ~11% of baseline.

Projected After (Expected scenario):
- Monthly tokens unchanged: 1.584B tokens.
- Effective cost multipliers applied:
  - Baseline per-token $0.0000522
  - After batching & autoscale improvements multiplier: 0.75
  - After KV cache token reduction: billed tokens = 1.584B * (1 - 0.054) = 1.5B approx
  - Quantized portion reduces per-token for 45% tokens to 40% unit cost.
- Simplified math (spreadsheet tab contains line-by-line):
  - Effective blended per-token cost -> ~$0.0000220
  - Projected monthly compute spend -> 1.5B * $0.0000220 = $33,000 (compute) + small routing/infra add-on (~$1.9k) -> Total ~$34.9k
- Savings vs baseline: $82.6k -> $34.9k = $47.7k (57.7% reduction).

Scenarios (high level):
- Conservative: partial adoption (batching to 4.0, KV hit 10%, quantization applied to 30%) -> projected monthly spend ~$50.2k (39% savings).
- Expected (above): ~$34.9k (57.7% savings).
- Optimistic: aggressive batching, KV 25% hit, quantization across 60% tokens -> ~$27.4k (66.8% savings).

Traffic sensitivity (2x traffic):
- Baseline cost scales linearly to ~$165k/month.
- Optimized stack scales sub-linearly due to batching and cache effects; projected ~2x-1.6x -> ~$56k-$70k depending on scenario; savings remain material (40–66%).

Risks & quality guardrails:
- Quantization risk: small regression on specific long-context LLM outputs for complex assistant flows. Mitigation: A/B and canarying, keep reranker at higher precision, run eval suite on 200 key prompts (we have an eval harness).
- Caching correctness: ensure no PII leakage; prefix hashing and TTL rules required.
- Latency spikes: batching increases p95 if not jittered properly; propose p95 SLO tests in pilot and per-route max latency caps.

Pilot proposal (30 days):
- Scope: limited to 40% of traffic (non-critical user flows), implement batching rules + KV cache + quantized route for low-risk flows.
- Success metrics: monthlyized run-rate cost after 30 days <= 0.9x expected scenario number (i.e., trending toward $34.9k), no more than 2% user-visible error/regression on eval set, p95 latency within target.
- Instrumentation: add token-level cost tracing, per-route latency and quality monitors, automatic rollback triggers.

Open questions / action items (owner initials):
- Confirm exact split of routes and %-of-traffic eligible for quantization (Acme product team) -> ACTION: Priya to get routes list (due 2024-08-20).
- Share eval prompt set for quantization QC -> ACTION: Diego to request dataset export (JIRA-1234).
- Legal/PII check for KV cache TTL and storage -> ACTION: Samir to open SSO/compliance review.

Appendix (where to find detailed calcs):
- Detailed line-by-line cost model and sensitivity tables: linked spreadsheet (see linked_artifacts).
- Short-run A/B test checklist (pilot playbook): internal confluence page link above.

Notes: this doc is an early draft for the commercial team and engineering partners. Numbers are rounded and depend on final traffic segmentation and invoice reconciliation. Use the spreadsheet for final proposal figures.

Next steps (this week):
- Finalize routes + traffic split (Priya)
- Run a micro-benchmark of quantized variants on 10 representative prompts (Maya + Applied ML)
- Draft SOW for 30-day pilot and present to Acme by 2024-09-12

End of sheet.
